decisions.text: Both remedies the trouble named: --supersedes for the act, and refusing a D<n>-shaped step label for the misreading. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Clause 2 narrowed: decide() refuses a ^D\d+$ step only when the line's text names that same D<n> as replaced or superseded, naming --supersedes; any other D<n> step lands as today. Census 2026-10-11: 1779/6398 gaps carry a D<n> step, 1039 decision lines landed at one, and the CLI's gap printout advises it. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

'Names D<n> as replaced or superseded' is exactly: re.search(rf"\b(replac(?:es|ed|ing)|supersed(?:es|ed|ing))\s+D{n}\b", text, re.I) or re.search(rf"\bD{n}\b(?:'s)?\s+(?:is\s+|are\s+)?(?:replaced|superseded)\b", text, re.I), n the step's digits. Measured 2026-10-11 over the live corpus: it catches 6 standing lines, all the 996668 shape (e.g. cff5a197b3c4 D32 'D1 IS REPLACED'), against 99 for a bare word-plus-id match. With supersedes given, this refusal does not apply. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

decide(ticket, step, line, *, by, root=None, supersedes=None): after the existing lacks, when supersedes is given, factor retire()'s lack checks into a module function _retire_lacks(doc, tk, want, by, because, into, exclude) that retire() also calls (exclude=None), and call it with the new entry's n as into and the new line excluded from the 'still cites' scan (the new line is not yet on the plan, so it is simply not in the scan); because is 'superseded by D<new n>'. Any lack raises Refused naming every lack and writes nothing. Then stamp each retired dict {by, at, because, into: new n}, ticket_log.append_log each (kind decision_retired, as retire()), remove them from the plan, append the new entry, and call _write_ticket ONCE. Without supersedes decide() behaves as today. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

__main__.py: p.add_argument('--supersedes', action='append', metavar='D<n>') (repeatable); valid only with --decide (else p.error); parsed with _decision_id; passed as supersedes=[...] to R.decide; on success it also prints 'retired D<n> into D<new>' per id. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

The proof is written red-first at cairn: cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_a_decision_supersedes_in_one_act.py, PROVES {'c70eeeef73ac': {'1','2'}}; tooth 1 counts _write_ticket calls by swapping R._write_ticket (must be 1) and reads D4 off the log retired into D5; tooth 2 is (2a) the 996668 shape refused naming --supersedes with the ticket bytes unchanged and (2b) 'D4 holds: ...' at step D4 landing. Both red 2026-10-11. test_a_superseded_decision_is_retired.py stays green (its decide at step D3 does not name D3 as replaced). CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
